title: Heisenberg Scaling in Many-Body Kinetic Uncertainty Relation via Quantum Feedback
summary: Kinetic uncertainty relations impose a fundamental constraint on counting precision by requiring large dynamical activity to suppress fluctuations. For $N$ independent constituents, the activity is additive and scales as $O(N)$, so the corresponding precision bound improves only as $O(1/N)$. A central question is whether many-body quantum systems can instead achieve Heisenberg scaling, with relative variance suppressed as $O(1/N^{2})$. Such scaling could enable substantially enhanced precision in quantum devices, including quantum clocks. Superradiance appears to provide a natural route…
